drivingQuestion: Why does the baraita single out the poor-gifts mitzvot when instructing a convert?
outcomeNote: the reason is supplied from R' Yoḥanan's dictum about Noahide theft

segments.he: וּמוֹדִיעִים אוֹתוֹ עֲוֹן לֶקֶט שִׁכְחָה וּפֵאָה וּמַעְשַׂר עָנִי. מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בֶּן נֹחַ נֶהֱרָג עַל פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה — וְלֹא נִיתָּן לְהִשָּׁבוֹן.
segments.en: The baraita continues: «And they inform him» of «the sin» of neglecting the mitzva to allow the poor to take «gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and» produce in the «corner» of one’s field, «and» about the «poor man’s tithe.» The Gemara asks: «What is the reason» to specifically mention these mitzvot? «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» Because «a gentile is executed» even «on account of» stealing «less than the value of a peruta,» since gentiles are particular about even such a small loss, «and» an item that a gentile steals «is not subject to being returned,» i.e., he is not obligated to return it to its owner. Since gentiles are unwilling to separate even from items of little value, a potential convert must be made aware that if he converts, he will be required to relinquish some of his property to others.
